newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian airlines eye Frankfurt cargo fees offer.
newsitem.headline: Asian airlines eye Frankfurt cargo fees offer.

text.p: Asian airlines are showing interest in an offer by Frankfurt airport to charge half price landing fees for cargo planes arriving between midnight and 0700 local(2200 and 0500 gmt), the airport's Hong Kong, China, Taiwan and Vietnam representative, Stephen Miller said.

Leading Asian carriers, including Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd, Air China, Thai Airways International, Singapore Airlines and Malaysian Airlines System, have been offered the scheme, Miller told Reuters.

"There are a number of airlines interested although I haven't seen any commitments yet. But these things take time when airlines plan at least a season ahead. We should see something happening by the end of October and the start of the winter season," Miller said.
Industry observers said Frankfurt has a reputation for being expensive but cargo operators on tight margins are expected to be wooed by cut-price rates for operating at night.

Miller declined to detail the scale of landing fees at Frankfurt but recent statistics issued by the International Air Transport Association (IATA) said it cost around US$8,300 to land a Boeing 747-400 at Frankfurt with a four hour turnround.

Miller said a curfew is still officially enforced but exceptions are being made for cargo flights. Because Frankfurt airport is sensitive to complaints about noise, only quieter "Chapter Three" aircraft will be allowed.
More night operations are also expected to free day time landing slots and ease congestion for passenger flights. Frankfurt is also keen to fully utilise its CargoCity development, Miller added.

"Night operations tie in quite well with both operators from the Far East and USA. It means airlines can get a much higher utilisation from their aircraft as well as a 50 per cent reduction in landing fees.
For cargo operators that can make a lot of difference to profitability," Miller said.
